conviction_note: The street models Q3 at about $25.6M, a 12% drop from Q2's $29.1M. Management said on 6 Aug that it had cut its assumed seasonal step-down, had added backup REMS teams and saw no early slowdown. A Q3 near $27M would therefore be a beat and would imply a raise to the FY guide on a name that paid +22.5% and +23.6% for its last two clear beats. Against that sit 340B price erosion, flagged margin and manufacturing-cost risk and only two to three weeks of visibility behind the comment, so p_up is 58. Over a 13-point absolute move that gives +2.1, close to the findings' +1.7 sum.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus is $25.63M with EPS -$0.10 (Earnings Whispers, https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/DCTH, and the 2026-11-02 preview at https://finviz.com/news/413406/delcath-faces-a-seasonality-test-as-street-braces-for-sequential-revenue-dip-and-loss). Benzinga shows $25.8M and Chartmill $26.5M, so the sources agree within about 3%. The company guides FY2026 revenue to $104-108M (Q2 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000872912/000162828026053902/dcth-q22026erex991.htm). H1 was $54.1M, which leaves $49.9-53.9M for H2, about $25-27M a quarter, so the $25.6M consensus sits inside, near the bottom of, the guided path.
positioning_check: Short interest: 1,883,018 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 6.24 days to cover, about 5.4% of 34.7M shares outstanding. That is down from 1,947,041 shares (5.37 days) at 2026-09-30 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dcth/shortinterest, read 2026-11-06). Borrow fee was about 0.4% at the June settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/dcth/). This is not a crowded short. The baseline carries no 25-delta skew (null). The put/call open-interest ratio is 0.12, so open interest is call-heavy, but total open interest is only 2,098 contracts and the ATM spread is 33% of mid, so the chain is thin. The event-implied move is 16.06%. Holders: BlackRock filed a 13G at 6.3% as of 2026-09-30. Rosalind (about 3.39M shares) distributed 27.5k shares in kind to LPs on 2026-10-13.

findings.finding: On the Q2 2026 call (6 Aug) management made four points on Q3. The CFO said guidance 'modestly reduced the seasonal step-down we had assumed for the third and fourth quarters', and backup REMS teams were trained at high-volume centers to avoid the staff-absence capacity loss behind the Q3 2025 miss. The CEO said 'this time last year we saw some softness... We're not seeing that quite yet', with two to three weeks of visibility. He also said Q2 new-patient starts (about 0.5 per site per month across 31 sites, 37 targeted by year-end) feed back-half volume because treatment courses run up to three quarters. Consensus of $25.63M still models a 12% sequential drop from $29.1M, close to the 15% Q2-to-Q3 drop of 2025 ($24.2M to $20.6M), the quarter management says it has fixed. A Q3 near $27M would be a beat of about 5%. It would also leave Q4 needing only about $23-27M to hit the $104-108M FY guide, which points to a raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-06): revenue $29.1M against a $26.0M consensus (+12%) plus a guide raise, and the stock rose 22.49%. Q1 2025 (2025-05-08), a beat: +23.64%. Q3 2025 seasonal miss with a guide cut: -4.59% on the 2025-10-20 pre-release and -4.62% on the 2025-11-04 print. Q4 2025 / FY26 guide (2026-02-26): -11.85%. The name pays for beat-and-raise and is sold on guide disappointment.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market believed seasonality was fixed, consensus would sit near the $27-29M run-rate rather than modelling a 12% sequential dip, and the stock would not have faded from its $17.42 post-Q2 high to $14-15. It is at $14.88, about 14% below the 52-week high, with 20-day run-up of -3.1%. The 2026-11-02 preview frames the print as a 'seasonality test' and puts consensus below last quarter, so the street has not taken management's word.
findings.independence: Partly independent. The 2026-11-02 preview at https://finviz.com/news/413406/... records the same management claim and the consensus dip, so it is the same underlying statement. Shares the guide arithmetic with the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000872912/000162828026053902/dcth-q22026erex991.htm), which reports roughly 30% volume growth. No third-party volume series was found.

findings.finding: Revenue per kit and margin are under pressure. The CFO said 340B discounts cut the effective ASP from about $185k to $170-173k per kit in 2026, so revenue grows about 21% while volume grows about 30%. She also warned that higher back-half manufacturing costs could take a quarter's gross margin 'a little bit below that 90%' (FY guide 86-89%). Q2 R&D was $10.4M against $6.9M a year earlier, and SG&A $13.4M against $11.4M, as breast and colorectal trials scale; the preview reports trial enrolment below plan. Volume strength therefore converts to less revenue and margin, and a dip below 90% gross margin is a plausible print-day headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed 90% gross margin (86% a year earlier), but adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.6M from $9.8M on opex growth, and the stock still rose 22.5% on the revenue beat and guide raise. Margin and opex have not been the line that moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. EPS consensus of -$0.10 already embeds a sharp margin and opex step, since Q2 was +$0.07. Kept small because a sub-90% gross margin line or a trial-enrolment shortfall on the call is a possible negative read on the day.
findings.independence: Same transcript as finding 1. The opex numbers are from the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000872912/000162828026053902/dcth-q22026erex991.htm). Enrolment below plan is from the 2026-11-02 preview (https://finviz.com/news/413406/...).

findings.finding: Unlike 2025, Delcath filed no preliminary Q3 release. EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-08-14 (item 5.03) and no item 2.02 since the Q2 print on 2026-08-06. In 2025 the company pre-released Q3 on 2025-10-20, a miss followed by a guide cut, and it pre-released Q4 on 2026-01-12. The absence of an October 2026 pre-release is weak evidence that there was no miss of the size that prompted last year's warning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2025-10-20 pre-release of a Q3 miss moved the stock -4.59%. The 2026-01-12 Q4 pre-release moved it +1.26%.
findings.why_not_priced: Anyone can see on EDGAR that no 8-K was filed, so this is likely priced as a non-warning. Kept small because it is an inference from absence; pre-releases are discretionary and last year's may have been tied to the miss.
findings.independence: The baseline's 8-K item 2.02 history (2025-10-20 and 2026-01-12 entries, none in Oct 2026) shows the same thing from the same source, EDGAR.

findings.finding: Rosalind Advisors, an insider-designated holder with directors on the board (about 3.39M shares after the transaction), distributed 27,502 shares in kind to limited partners on 2026-10-13 to meet redemption requests, and converted 36.27 Series E preferred into 3,627 shares. A 13D/A followed on 2026-10-19. The supply is small, under 0.1 day of average volume per tranche, but it signals LP redemptions at a large holder.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record for this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Public Form 4, but immaterial in size. Filed at near zero for completeness. A larger redemption wave would show up as further Form 4s, and none was found.
findings.independence: 13D/A index at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/872912/000162262726000027/, from the same filer. outside_window.finding: IDEAYA/Servier darovasertib plus crizotinib (OptimUM-02: PFS 6.9 vs 3.1 months, HR 0.42) is under NDA under RTOR for first-line HLA-A2-negative metastatic uveal melanoma, with filing completion guided to H2 2026. An approval would add a systemic competitor in HEPZATO's indication. No decision is dated inside the window.
Year-end treatment-center target of 37 (31 at July 2026). Achievement is only visible in Q4 or FY results, though the call may update the count.

baseline_tension: No skew is available, and call-heavy but thin open interest neither confirms nor contradicts the lean. The 20-day run-up of -3.1% with +6% over 5 days and the fade from the post-Q2 high mean the market has not priced in management's seasonality claim, so a positive lean cuts mildly against the recent tape rather than following it.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (inference from absence and proxies): the no-pre-release finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the bar is sourced from three agreeing estimate sources plus the company guide; consensus sits inside the guided path, so finding 1 is filed as a guidance finding (the raise is the payoff), not a reported-quarter beat alone; no cap applied
Lesson 1 (reaction function): history shows beats with raises paid +22% to +24%, so no veto on the positive; p_up stays at 58 because the visibility behind management's claim was two to three weeks
Lesson 7: short interest checked (5.4%, 6.2 days, not crowded), so the small negatives were not shrunk further
